evidence: Plaut. Truc. 4.4.31: dīcere hīc quidvīs licet (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Heaut. 4.1.28: quidvīs satis est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: As an adjective, quīvīs, quaevīs, quodvīs: quōvīs modō, in any way at all (Sall. J. 11.9, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.12–13: cum quidlibet ille garrīret (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Often a little slighting: just anything, the first thing that comes (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: pictōribus atque poētīs quidlibet audendī semper fuit aequa potestās
phrases.english: painters and poets have always had an equal right to dare anything

sources: Lewis & Short: quivis · Lewis & Short: quilibet
Horace quoted as Lewis & Short cites him (s.v. quilibet: A. P. 9).
